_note: EXTERIOR round 1, 2026-08-22. Room 11 'Frontyard' is not a room: it is the front of the house, and the only view it is ever seen from is the whole-house level ('all'), where the app hides generated room geometry and shows the shell GLB instead. SHOOT WITH --level all, NEVER --level 1: a level-1 shot drops into single-floor mode, which hides the shell, the lawn and the trees and shows a studio backdrop. Build scripts: scratchpad/ext/ (kit.py shared helpers, f_porch.py this room, b_deck.py + b_furn.py room 3, pick.py pixel->world probe). Most of this yard is NOT placed objects - it is procedural geometry in frontend/js/environment.js (addGroundCover + addFrontYard), which is the right home for anything that has to be visible on the whole-house view and costs no GLB payload.

_room._rect_warning: The traced rect does NOT line up with the shell. The shell's porch is at x -7..20.3, z 29.5..40.6 and its floor is at world y 2.13 - 5.87 ft BELOW the first-floor group that objects hang off. Every placement here therefore uses pos.y = 2.13 - 8.0 = -5.87. Anchor to the shell, not to this rect.

_environment_js._note: The bulk of the front yard is procedural. Rewritten this round against MEASURED shell landmarks; the previous version derived them as offsets from the roof rect and put the whole front bed 4-5 ft out on the lawn.
_environment_js.addGroundCover: grass over the shell's pale site pad at both of its heights, with sloped bank quads clothing the 2 ft vertical faces between them. Runs 4 ft past the pad's own front edge - anything short leaves a white sliver reading as a kerb across the lawn.
_environment_js.driveway: poured slab x 20.8..47.1, z 29.5..75.4 with one longitudinal control joint and transverse joints every 12.5 ft, plus the walk from the porch steps to the drive
_environment_js.slate_course: dry-stacked thin-slab retaining wall along the pad's front face (z 41, x -10.2..10.9) and its west face (x -10.1, z -4.9..41). This is the property's signature hardscape and it is also what turns the GLB's bare 2 ft white cliff into a wall.
_environment_js.front_bed: river rock at the foot of the slate (x -10.4..11.0, z 41.5..47.4) with a near-continuous clipped-boxwood row, drifts of purple perennials and four flagstones stepping up to the porch steps
_environment_js.east_bed: rock bed along the property line east of the drive with boxwood/perennials and two squat path lights
_environment_js.island_bed: bed at the street end of the drive with the lamp post and three ornamental grass clumps
_environment_js.props: black SUV nose-in on the drive, BLUE wheeled bin against the garage's east corner, two black urns at the porch/garage junction
_environment_js.trees: three mature framing canopies (new addShadeTree scales height with s; addDeciduous does not, which capped the whole treeline at shrub height), plus a woodland line across the far side of the street
_environment_js.neighbour: a two-garage-door house massing to the west, as in the front photograph

_metrics._pose: front photo-matched: pos [34,5.5,92] target [15,13,30] fov 48 - the camera settles at y 15.5, the app clamps it

driveway.verdict: match on value, spread AND fine-scale gradient

river_rock.verdict: value close, still 3x too smooth - see _open

_open: River rock meters mean|d1| 5.5 against the photograph's 15.8. Real river rock is a dense field of individually lit stones; ours is a speckled plane with scattered cobbles at one per 2 sq ft. Raising density further is the obvious lever but it is geometry, not texture - a cobble normal-map on the beds material would be the cheaper fix.

The shell GLB has a Sketchup SCALE FIGURE baked into its merged Root_Node mesh at about x -16.5, z 44.7. It cannot be hidden separately (Root_Node is 79k triangles covering the whole model). The west framing tree is deliberately planted over it.
Beds are rectangles; the photographed beds curve. environment.js has no polygon bed primitive.
